summary.en: An Act to provide for the control of dealings in rubber 4of 1920

heading.en: Collection, purchase and storage to be under rubber

text.en: No person shall, unless duly licensed in that behalf, Collection, tap rubber on State land, purchase rubber, or keep any purchase and place for the treatment and storage of rubber: Provided that a licence to tap rubber includes the right to treat the same, and a licence to purchase rubber includes the right to keep a place to store the same.

(1) Subject to such fees as His Majesty in Council may by rule from time to time direct, the licensing officer may issue licences to tap rubber on State land, to purchase or to store and treat rubber.

(2) Every licence shall be for one year or such shorter period as the licensing officer may determine.

(3) No licence shall be transferable.

(1) Every licensed dealer shall keep books of account entered the date of purchase of any rubber, and address of the seller, the weight and description of rubber purchased, and the price.

(2) Every licensee shall on the demand of any licensing officer produce for inspection all books kept by him the provisions of this section and allow copies to be made.

(3) Every such book shall be preserved by the licensee for one year from the date of its last being used for the making of any entry therein.

licens~d dealer shall deliver to every person from whom he purchases rubber a receipt showing the date of purchase, the name of the vendor, and the weight and description of the rubber purchased. on 7. (1) Every person who cultivates rubber on alienated land shall before he commences to tap such rubber inform land the licensing officer, who shall if necessary visit the land and shall issue to such person a certificate showing the number of the title, the name of the owner, and the number of trees tapped, and shall indorse from time to time on such certificate any alterations that may be required.

(2) Any person contravening this section shall be on conviction to a fine of $250.

Except as provided in section 7 any person contraven-Penalties Act shall be liable to a fine of $1,000 and any person contravening the provisions of any rules made under this Act shall be liable to a fine of $500.
